items.title: Influence of traffic speed and acoustic environment on perception and perceived workload in virtual reality
items.summary: In a virtual urban park, 34 participants rated 30 km/h traffic as more pleasant and less eventful than 50 km/h traffic across three acoustic contexts. The context also affected both soundscape dimensions, while the measured difference in perceived workload was not significant.

items.title: Restorative urban soundscapes
items.summary: This review links acoustic scenes and perceptual processing to physiological, cognitive, and subjective restoration. It argues that restorative effects depend on perceived meaning, audiovisual congruence, listener and cultural differences, and measurement choices, and calls for conditional, testable design recommendations rather than generic prescriptions to add natural sounds.

items.title: Absorbing exceptional point of coherent vortex beams
items.summary: Experiments with acoustic vortex beams and symmetry-tailored metasurfaces realised chiral coherent-perfect-absorption exceptional points. Rotating the metasurface switched absorption capacity and degenerate states, while the vortex beams’ orbital-angular-momentum channels increased channel capacity and enabled sensitivity alongside robust perfect absorption.

items.title: Single-particle limit of a topological edge state in a locally resonant band gap
items.summary: A theoretical and numerical study adds a local resonator to an SSH-inspired stiffness dimer. Matching a topological edge state to the resonator-induced attenuation singularity confines the mode to one boundary particle at low frequency; boundary tuning can recover this idealised state after disorder detunes it.
